The most likely buggy method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.traverseObjectLiteral(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.FlowScope)`

Why:
- The failure is an unexpected type widening inside the object literal passed to `temp3`.
- The call-site warning shows the literal is inferred as:
  `{b: boolean, n: number, text: (string|undefined)}`
  even though the literal clearly provides `text: 'a string'`.
- That means the bug happens before call checking, during inference of the object literal’s property types.
- `TypeCheck.visitCall` / `visitParameterList` only report the mismatch; they do not create the bad type.
- In `TypeInference.traverseObjectLiteral`, each property type is read from the value expression and then installed onto the inferred object type. This is exactly where `text` should remain `string`.
- There is a suspicious line in that method:
  `var.setType(oldType == null ? valueType : oldType.getLeastSupertype(oldType));`
  The merge uses `oldType.getLeastSupertype(oldType)`, which ignores `valueType` entirely. That is almost certainly wrong and indicates broken type propagation for object literal properties / qualified slots. Even if this is not the only issue, this method is the clearest source of incorrect object-literal inference.

Most likely diagnosis:
- The object literal inference logic is incorrectly widening or preserving a previously widened property type for `text`, causing it to become `(string|undefined)` instead of `string`.
- The erroneous merge/update behavior in `TypeInference.traverseObjectLiteral` is the strongest candidate root cause.
- The warning at `temp3(...)` is just the symptom surfaced later by parameter checking.
